In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a new model of reinforcement learning with rich, sequential observations, and we design and analyze an algorithm for this model that is the first to achieve sample-efficient, model-free, and model-based learning.
the algorithm learns to behave near optimally after a number of trials that is polynomial in the relevant parameters, logarithm in the number of polices, and independent of observation space.

the proposed method can be used for solving a variety of sequential decision making problems with a small number of states and predictable reward functions, including problems that are not Markovian, and problems where the observation space is large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a theoretical justification for the use of function approximation in reinforcement learning, in particular in the case of rich observations.
we have designed a model for sequential decision making with rich observations, and we have developed a sample efficient reinforcement learning algorithm to solve the model.
we have designed a new reinforcement learning model, PAC reinforcement learning, and we have proposed a new reinforcement learning method, Least Squares Policy Iteration, for solving this new model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reinforcement learning can be sample-efficient in a wide range of settings, even with rich observations and general reactive function classes.
reinforcement learning with rich observation is possible in a wide range of settings, and can be done efficiently with function approximation.

the key to efficient reinforcement learning is to focus on the right class of problems, and to design algorithms that can learn from the right kind of data, namely the data that is available in practice.
